blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal. The reports count condos and townhomes together in one line, so this table cannot separate the two. Shares are this community’s count divided by the Burnaby total for condos and townhomes that month.

blocks.text: Listings of condos and townhomes in Montecito rose from 11 in June to 12 in September, and 7 sold across the 4 months. In September the community held 0.9% of Burnaby’s 1,333 condos and townhomes listed.
Condos and townhomes or houses in Montecito?
Montecito also had 20 houses listed and 2 sold in September, against 12 condos and townhomes listed. The Montecito houses page has those figures.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Montecito?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 12 condos and townhomes listed in Montecito. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Montecito a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?
faq.a: In September 2026, condos and townhomes in Montecito had a sales ratio of not published for the month. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Montecito from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 7 condos and townhomes sold in Montecito over those 4 months, out of 750 in all of Burnaby.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.
